chat_hint: Write as a customer in any supported language. Rules decide if the AI may answer; money, legal, GDPR and angry messages go to a person.
dec_empty: Send a message to see the triage decision, the EU261 check and the handoff note.
t_hint: Paste the booking confirmation or the text under a boarding-pass barcode, or upload a photo (photos need a vision model).
x_hint: Check and correct the fields, add what happened, then run the check or draft the letter.
r_hint: Paste the airline's refusal. The agent names the cause, maps it to EU case law and suggests the next step. A claims handler always decides.
a_empty: The cause, the recommendation and the reasoning appear here.
l_hint: Fill in by hand, or come here from the ticket reader. Amounts and articles come from the check, never from the model.
lo_empty: The draft appears here. A person reviews and sends it.
footer: Demo for a flight-compensation claims service. Simplified EU261 rules, not legal advice.
holding: Thanks, I've passed this to a colleague who will reply personally within one business day. You don't need to send anything else for now.
elig_ask: I can run a quick EU261 check for you. Please tell me: {need}.
elig_yes: Good news: your flight {route} ({km} km) looks eligible. Compensation would be EUR {amount} per passenger, before our service fee. This is a preliminary check, not a guarantee. To start the claim, send your boarding pass or e-ticket.
elig_no: From what you've told me, this flight is probably not eligible: {reason} If any detail is different, tell me and I'll check again.
fee: We work on a no win, no fee basis. If we get your compensation, our fee is 30% (VAT included). If the airline refuses and the case has to go to court or an external lawyer, the fee is 50%. Baggage and reimbursement claims are 40%.
status: Every claim moves through these stages: submitted, sent to the airline (a reply usually takes 2-8 weeks), negotiation, and if needed a national authority or court. I can't promise a date, but a colleague can tell you the exact stage of your claim if you share your claim number.
documents: To start a claim we need: the boarding pass or e-ticket for every passenger, an ID document for the lead passenger, and a signed authorisation so we can act for you. You can upload them in your claim form.
m_what: what happened (delay, cancellation or denied boarding)
m_delay: how many hours late you arrived at the final destination
m_airline: the airline (flights into the EU are covered only on EU airlines)
rs_not_covered: the route is not covered by EU261 (departure outside the EU on a non-EU airline).
rs_extraordinary: the airline cites extraordinary circumstances, so a colleague needs to review the evidence.
rs_under_3h: the arrival delay was under 3 hours.
rs_notice_14d: the cancellation was announced 14 or more days before departure.
rs_likely: Likely eligible: EUR {amount} per passenger before the service fee.
ib_hint: The agent sorts a batch of messages in 20 languages: what it answers itself, what goes to a person and why. Rules only, no LLM, so it is instant and free.
ib_ph: Paste your own messages, one per line
ib_open: Click a row to open it in the chat.
ib_empty: Run the sample inbox to see how the agent sorts the mail.
hw_intro: Rules decide, the LLM only writes. That keeps answers safe, cheap and predictable.
hw_s2: Triage rules: money, legal threats, GDPR and angry customers go straight to a person.
hw_s3: Extracts the flight facts; the EU261 amount is computed by code, not by the model.
hw_s4: A small, cheap LLM writes the reply from the knowledge base and the computed check.
hw_s5: Number guard: if the reply contains a number that is not in the facts, the model gets one retry, then a safe template is used.
hw_cost: Works with any OpenAI-compatible model (here Groq gpt-oss-20b) and runs offline with templates when no key is set.
elig_total: For {n} passengers that is EUR {total} in total.
too_old: The flight is over 2 years old. Claim deadlines depend on the country, so a colleague checks this case.
m_future: the date of a flight that has already taken place (this date is in the future)
rs_halved: Likely eligible: EUR {amount} per passenger before the service fee. It is half the usual amount because the replacement flight arrived within {h} hours.
elig_half: It is half the usual amount because the replacement flight arrived within {h} hours.
rs_voluntary: you gave up your seat voluntarily, and volunteers get the benefits agreed with the airline rather than EU261 compensation.
